messages.subject: gdistsamp error caused by large number of NAs?
parts:
I am trying to run gdistsamp to look at line transects of 30 sites that have been surveyed over 32 different time periods. I keep getting this error.

null = gdistsamp(~1, ~1, ~1, umf)
Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) : 
  initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite

and I've tried setting different start values and it hasn't changed anything. From reading through others posts it seems that my problem might be because of the large number of NAs I have (none of my transects were run in all 32 time periods). Though I haven't seen that specifically confirmed anywhere.

Can anyone confirm if that could be the cause of the problem?

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] gdistsamp error caused by large number of NAs?
parts:
hi Auriel,
 
 I'll bet this is just due to poor starting values.  I dont know what to say to help get better starting values but try setting some of them to extreme values in the parameter space and see what happens.  Most often this result happens when sigma is relatively large so that the default starting value (0 I think on the log scale) is way off.
 
 Another option is to try a subset of the sites where you have quality data and lots of observations and see if you can get estimates from that subset of sites to use as starting values.
 
regards
andy

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] gdistsamp error caused by large number of NAs?
parts:
Another option is to try a different mixture model or key function.  You were using the default on both, because you didn't specify either in the function call.

If one of those models works, you can then use those parameter estimates as starting values for the model you were trying to run.

Cheers,
Chris

parts:
I took a subset of my data with less NAs and I'm having the same problem.

When I run a halfnorm, uniform or exp key function

Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) : 
  initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite

Hazard key function returns this error

Error in integrate(gxhaz, db[j], db[j + 1], shape = shape[i, t], scale = scale,  : 
  non-finite function value

If I'm interpreting those errors correctly it's the same error with different words. I get the same errors using a negative binomial and Poisson mixture though I believe it's the NB that I actually want. 

I've been reading all morning trying to figure out how to input start values, since that seems to be my problem, but I can't get any models to run so I can't pull the values from there. I've tried a wide variety of values for starting values and I keep getting the same errors.

Can anyone provide some help on how to input start values? or maybe there is something else that I am missing.

Hi,

I'm having the same problem with gdistsamp and I was wondering if anyone had ever solved this thread? My data has 5 primary periods and a lot of NA values, and when I try to run the model I get the error: "Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) :   initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite".  I tried again on a smaller sample dataset with 2 primary periods and 5 sites; when I set 2 sites equal to NA for 1 primary period each, I get the error, but if I have no NAs it runs fine.  I've played around with starting values but nothing seems to work.

Thanks for your help,

Lucretia
